title: When Bigger Becomes Brittle: Why Compression Hurts More as Language Models Scale
abstract: arXiv:2611.07891v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Quantization and pruning reduce the cost of deploying language models, but their effects are usually reported as benchmark scores. Such scores record only the loss that remains at the output. Inside the model, compression damages some components more than others, and the rest of the network can partly compensate. The observed loss therefore reflects both the damage and this compensation, which benchmark scores cannot separate. How the two combine, and whether their balance changes with model size, remains unclear. We study this compensation for in-context retrieval, a capability carried by a small, identifiable set of attention heads. To separate the two, the expected loss from ablating these heads is decomposed exactly into the part restored by the rest of the network, attributed to the components responsible, and the part that reaches the output. translated_title: 当变大变得脆弱：为什么语言模型规模越大，压缩带来的伤害越严重
translated_abstract: 量化与剪枝可以降低语言模型的部署成本，但它们的效果通常以基准测试分数来报告。这类分数只记录了输出端剩余的损失。而在模型内部，压缩对某些组件的破坏程度大于其他组件，网络的其余部分可以部分补偿这种破坏。因此，观察到的损失同时反映了破坏本身和这种补偿，而基准测试分数无法将两者区分开来。这两者如何共同作用，以及它们的平衡关系是否随模型规模而变化，目前仍不清楚。我们针对上下文检索能力研究了这种补偿机制，该能力由一小组可识别的注意力头承载。为了将破坏与补偿分离，我们精确地将消融这些注意力头所产生的预期损失分解为两个部分：一部分由网络其余部分恢复（并归因于负责补偿的具体组件），另一部分则真正传递到输出端。随后，我们将这一分解在不同模型规模之间进行比较。对于规模相当的破坏，较小的模型……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出一种精确的分解方法，将压缩（量化/剪枝）造成的损失拆分为“网络其余部分的补偿恢复”与“真正传递到输出的残余损失”两部分，并发现随着语言模型规模增大，网络内部的补偿能力减弱，因此压缩对大模型的伤害反而更严重。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an exact decomposition of compression-induced loss into the part compensated by the rest of the network and the part that reaches the output, revealing that compensation weakens as language models scale, making larger models more brittle under compression.
